clue.text: Conspicuous influence exerted by active troops

blocks.note: force is power or influence over events

explanation.surface: Troops on the move make their weight felt in a very visible way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like one description, but the first two words build the answer and the last two define it.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking force is a military unit kept ready to launch an attack, so its soldiers are troops in action.

clue.text: Vic left the Spice Girl after tart turned up in restaurant

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up means reading it from the bottom upwards
if one person has left another, he is gone from her, so those letters drop out

blocks.note: Victoria Beckham was Posh Spice in the pop group the Spice Girls
taken as written, the short form of a name

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of a man walking out on a pop star once a floozy appeared, set in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girl's first name happens to start with the man's name, so his leaving strips those three letters from her.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eating house serving simple food.

clue.text: Provoke fashionable hound

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A command to stir up a trendy dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur anger or a penalty is to bring it upon yourself, to call it forth by your actions.

clue.text: First capital?

blocks.note: first meaning: coming at the beginning
second meaning: the capital letter that begins a name

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a question about a country's first seat of government; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means occurring at the start, and as a noun it is the first letter of a name, usually written large.

clue.text: One speculating how to get better

definitions.text: One speculating how to get better

blocks.clueFragment: One speculating how to get better
blocks.note: surface reading: someone pondering how to recover from an illness
setter's reading: a better is a person who bets, and wagering is how you become one

explanation.surface: Someone wondering how to recover their health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like improving in health, but here it is one who places bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler takes risks on uncertain outcomes for money, which is speculation by another name.

clue.text: Work with the media or a slave-driver

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: A choice between a media career and running a chain gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A slave-driver treats people harshly and keeps them down, which is what an oppressor does.

clue.text: Cool, cool beginner on the up and up

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is whatever stands at its start

blocks.note: the opening letter of the second cool
a hill is ground that goes up and up

explanation.surface: A laid-back newcomer whose career is rising fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the up and up' is an idiom for steadily improving; it splits into 'on', placing C above, and 'the up and up', a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill something is to make it cold, and as a noun a chill is a coolness.

clue.text: Deadly kind of broadcasting?

blocks.note: surface reading: radio or television programmes so dull they bore you to death
setter's reading: a substance spreading lethal radiation all around it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' suggests the BBC, but it means scattering widely, and what is scattered here is radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: The decay of unstable atomic nuclei gives off ionising rays that can kill living tissue, sending them out in every direction.

clue.text: The point where the action is

blocks.note: first meaning: literally at the pointed tip of a blade or tool
second meaning: in the thick of things, on the front line

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about a lively place; split it and the point is the sharp end of a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in the most demanding, exposed part of an activity, and literally names a blade's tip.

clue.text: A coy sort of miss pointlessly promoting lawlessness

indicators.note: a point is a compass direction such as south, and without one the word loses that letter
a sort of something is a version of it, so the letters come in another arrangement

blocks.note: the indefinite article, in its form used before a vowel
arch means playfully knowing, a coy manner

explanation.surface: A demure young woman aimlessly championing disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS loses one S, a compass point, and MIS is rearranged; 'A' stands for AN, the other form of the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the political belief in abolishing government, which opponents equate with a state of no laws.

clue.text: Colour for cockney isn't soft originally

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so this piece is placed in front

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for soft
a Londoner's cockney speech says ain't for isn't

explanation.surface: A cockney insisting that a colour is not soft at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class dialect of East London, famous for ain't.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint is coloured liquid, and the word can mean colour itself, as in the paint on a car.

clue.text: Put to rest in Tintern Abbey

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following word

blocks.note: the run of letters between its first and last
surface padding completing the name of the Welsh ruin

explanation.surface: A burial at the ruined Welsh abbey.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintern Abbey is a ruined monastery in the Wye Valley in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body, and laying someone to rest is the euphemism for burial.

clue.text: Suffering this, I left with the hall spinning

indicators.note: something spinning is whirled round, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone so poorly that the room is whirling round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor health is a state of being unwell, of suffering from sickness.

clue.text: Publicity about North American student describing a gland

definitions.note: an adjective applied to a gland

blocks.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An advertising campaign about an American student who writes about anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal glands sit above the kidneys, so adrenal is the adjective naming that particular gland.

clue.text: Indifferent to broken egg in Lent

indicators.note: a broken thing has its parts scattered, so these letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone who does not care that eggs get smashed during the fast before Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: Lent is the Christian fast before Easter, when eggs were traditionally given up.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligent person fails to take proper care, showing a careless lack of concern.

clue.text: Artist upset class of rogues

indicators.note: upset things are knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter offended by a class of scoundrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascals are mischievous or dishonest people, so the plural matches scoundrels.

clue.text: Awful insult a boy mostly suffered when washing

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
something awful is a terrible mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lad taunted horribly while having his bath.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY loses its Y before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablutions is a formal word for the act of washing oneself.

clue.text: Wrest butane, for example, from riot controller?

blocks.note: to tear something away is to wrest it
butane is an example of a gas

explanation.surface: Seizing a fuel canister from someone policing a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas is the irritant police use to disperse rioting crowds, which makes it a means of control.

clue.text: Clipping trim animal

blocks.note: to snip is to cut or trim
a pet is a tame animal

explanation.surface: Grooming a sleek animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipping' and 'trim' look like grooming, but 'Clipping' is a noun: a cut-off scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece cut out, like a newspaper cutting.

clue.text: Firm to get under way with a flower show

blocks.note: to roll is to start moving, as in 'let's roll'

explanation.surface: A company launching an exhibition of blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower show' looks like a horticultural event; here it is the showy part of a single flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The corolla is a flower's ring of petals, the colourful display that attracts pollinators.

clue.text: Money in cane container for hot spice

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another
the following word is named as the vessel that holds the other piece

explanation.surface: Cash smuggled in a hollow cane meant for spices.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper ground into a fiery powder.

clue.text: Visibility is less, but including a prospect of being maintained

indicators.note: less means without, so the following word comes out
including means holding within, so a piece goes inside

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: poor visibility, but some hope of things holding up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visibility is less' reads as worsening fog, but it means VISIBILITY without IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Viability is the capacity to survive or keep going, the likelihood that a plan can be sustained.

clue.text: A French god's valediction

explanation.surface: A French deity bidding farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell, borrowed from French, and a valediction is a word of leave-taking.

clue.text: Ease pressure and put the Spanish back

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters from right to left

explanation.surface: Instructions to relax and return something Spanish to its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To let up is to slacken off, to stop pushing so hard.

clue.text: Tether student on drug to a tree

explanation.surface: A high student tied to a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A leash is a strap or cord that restrains an animal, which is what a tether does.

clue.text: Stumble? Third fielder? Rubbish!

indicators.note: third points at the letter in position three of the following word

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator despairing at a clumsy fielder at third man.
explanation.walkthrough: Third man is a cricket fielding position, which makes 'Third fielder' look like one player.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is cow's stomach lining, and colloquially it means worthless nonsense.

clue.text: Silly old stooge, one of a pair, in baggy trousers

definitions.text: one of a pair, in baggy trousers

blocks.note: first meaning: the foolish old man of Italian comic theatre, butt of the jokes

blocks.clueFragment: one of a pair, in baggy trousers
blocks.note: second meaning: one leg of a pair of loose, wide trousers

explanation.surface: A foolish old sidekick dressed in billowing trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantaloon is the doddering old man of the commedia dell'arte; his trousers gave their name to pantaloons.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock comic character is the dupe of the play, and the trousers named after him come as a pair.

clue.text: Test, touch each composition and get to the point

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Advice to an essay writer: check every piece and be direct.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from early films that skipped to the chase scene, means stop wasting time and address the main matter.
